high.title: Banking Sector Earnings Update (July 10): One Bank's Profit Estimated to Drop 50%, Management Warns of "Very Difficult" Situation as NPLs Could Surge
high.summary: Sacombank's CEO Loic Faussier issued a stark warning about the bank's H1 2026 performance, flagging a deeply stressed operating environment. Key concerns: net interest margin (NIM) compression, non-performing loan (NPL) ratio potentially spiking to 5.6%, and provisioning costs potentially hitting a record VND 4,700 billion — among the highest in the sector. Pre-tax profit is estimated at only VND 1,900–2,000 billion, down approximately 50% year-on-year, continuing a declining trend since early 2026. In contrast, ABBank reported a strong H1 2026 estimated profit of VND 3,016 billion, up ~80% YoY, signaling significant divergence within the sector.

high.title: If Crude Oil Falls Below $70/Barrel, What Will Vietnam's Average CPI Be in 2026?
high.summary: Vietnam's economy recorded robust H1 2026 GDP growth of 8.18%, with Q2 alone expanding 8.39% — the strongest Q2 print since 2011. Final consumption rose 8.15% and asset accumulation surged 15.2%, signaling strong domestic demand and investment momentum. However, this recovery has come alongside accelerating inflation: average H1 2026 CPI rose 4.38% YoY, well above the 3.27% recorded in the same period last year and the highest H1 reading in 12 years. While June CPI dipped 0.39% MoM on falling fuel prices, analysts caution that underlying inflationary pressures remain elevated.

high.title: Dragon Capital Forecasts Series of "Good News" for Vietnam's Stock Market Going Forward
high.summary:
Dragon Capital's H2 2026 strategy report presents a constructive outlook for Vietnamese equities, underpinned by three key catalysts. First, accelerated public investment and pro-growth fiscal policies are expected to sustain domestic demand momentum. Second — and critically for foreign capital flows — Vietnam is set to be officially upgraded by FTSE Russell to **Secondary Emerging Market status from September 2026**, a landmark event that should trigger significant passive and active fund inflows into VN-Index constituents. Third, current valuations are described as attractive.

On the macro side, Dragon Capital highlights Vietnam's resilience against external headwinds including oil price shocks and Fed tightening. H1 2026 GDP growth came in at **8.18%**, the strongest first-half reading since data collection began in 2011. Disbursed FDI reached **USD 13 billion (+11.2% YoY)**, while newly registered and supplementary FDI commitments hit **USD 34.7 billion** — a strong signal of sustained foreign investor confidence. The VN-Index has continued to reach new highs despite prolonged net foreign selling pressure.

high.title: Bank Deposit Rates as of July 11: MB, Sacombank, HDBank, Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, and Others
high.summary: Vietnamese deposit rates remain elevated as of July 11, with ACB leading the market at 7.3% p.a. for the 12-month tenor — the highest rate currently on offer across the surveyed institutions. Saigonbank follows closely at 7.2% p.a., while MBV, VCBNeo, PGBank, and VIB all post 7.0% p.a. for the same tenor. In total, six banks are now offering rates at or above 7.0% p.a. for 12-month deposits. The next tier — Bac A Bank, LPBank, BVBank, and OCB — clusters around 6.9% p.a. The four major state-owned banks (Agribank, BIDV, Vietcombank, VietinBank) hold steady at 6.8% p.a. for 12- and 18-month tenors, and 6.6% p.a. for 6- and 9-month tenors.

medium.title: Ha Tinh's Largest Gold Company Exposed: 68,000 Transactions Worth Up to VND 5,000 Billion But Only Paying VND 10–20 Million in Monthly Taxes
medium.summary:
Security investigative authorities in Ha Tinh Province have initiated criminal proceedings against Phuong Xuan Gold and Silver Joint Stock Company and two of its senior executives — the Chairwoman and Deputy Director — on charges of tax evasion under Article 200(3) of the Vietnamese Penal Code. The case involves approximately 68,000 transactions valued at up to VND 5,000 billion (~USD 196 million), against which the company reportedly remitted only VND 10–20 million per month in taxes — a stark and suspicious discrepancy. This case is of moderate relevance to macro traders as it signals heightened regulatory scrutiny over Vietnam's gold trading sector, which intersects directly with informal FX and monetary flows. Large-scale, under-reported gold transactions can act as a shadow channel for capital movement and USD demand, potentially influencing VND liquidity dynamics. Authorities indicate this crackdown is part of a broader initiative to tighten financial security oversight in precious metals markets. Investors should monitor whether enforcement actions expand to other gold dealers, as this could affect informal USD/gold hedging behavior and SBV's ability to control parallel FX market pressures.

---

medium.title: Gold Bar and Ring Prices Reverse Sharply Higher on July 10, Approaching VND 150 Million/Tael
medium.summary:
Domestic gold prices in Vietnam surged VND 900,000/tael on the morning of July 10, with SJC gold bars quoted at VND 146.9–149.9 million/tael, pushing the sell price back toward the psychologically significant VND 150 million threshold. Gold ring prices also rose, with SJC listing 24K rings at VND 145.7–148.7 million/tael. International spot gold was steady at approximately USD 4,127/ounce with limited intraday movement. The sharp domestic gold price move, despite muted global spot prices, suggests domestic demand and supply dynamics — including SBV's management of the gold market — remain a relevant factor for VND liquidity. Elevated domestic gold prices historically attract USD demand for import hedging and can create mild pressure on the VND/USD rate if sustained.

---

medium.title: H1 2026 Banking Sector Results Update: One Bank Reports 80% Profit Growth, VietinBank and Agribank Set New Records
medium.summary: Vietnam's banking sector continues to show robust momentum in H1 2026. ABBank reported estimated post-tax profit of VND 3,016 billion for the first six months, up 80% year-on-year and representing 67% of its full-year target of VND 4,500 billion. Total assets reached VND 260.65 trillion (100% of plan), with outstanding loans at VND 138 trillion and total mobilized funds at VND 163 trillion. Notably, NPL ratio is controlled at a low 0.55% and CAR exceeds 12%, signaling strong asset quality. VietinBank crossed the historic VND 3 quadrillion (3,000 trillion) total assets milestone — a first for the bank — while Agribank surpassed VND 2 quadrillion in outstanding loans. For bond and equity investors, these results confirm that credit growth remains healthy and system-wide asset quality is holding up, reducing near-term concerns about banking sector stress. Strong bank profitability also supports the case for stable deposit/lending rate spreads. Watch for full Q2 official filings to assess provisioning levels and net interest margin compression amid the low-rate environment.

medium.title: VietinBank, BIDV, and Vietcombank Shareholders Receive Good News
medium.summary: Vietnam's three largest state-owned commercial banks — VietinBank (CTG), BIDV (BID), and Vietcombank (VCB) — have announced cash dividend payments for fiscal year 2025. VietinBank's board approved a 4.5% cash dividend on par value (VND 450 per share), with record date set for July 24, 2026 and payment date August 27, 2026; the total payout amounts to VND 3,495 billion. BIDV and Vietcombank have made similar cash dividend announcements. For equity investors in Vietnamese financials, coordinated dividend payouts from the Big Three banks are a positive sentiment signal and reflect regulators' growing comfort with capital distribution after years of retained earnings pressure. The combined payout scale is also relevant for liquidity dynamics on the VN-Index, as institutional reallocation around ex-dividend dates can drive short-term volatility in bank stocks, which carry significant index weight.

medium.title: Vietnam's $100 Billion Agricultural Export Target: 'No Poverty Reduction Policy Works Better Than Connecting 9 Million Smallholder Farmers Directly to International Markets'
medium.summary: Vietnam has set an ambitious target of reaching $100 billion in agricultural, forestry, and fishery exports by end-2027, described as a "500-day campaign." Experts emphasize that achieving this goal hinges less on expanding cultivated acreage and more on integrating Vietnam's 9 million smallholder farming households into global supply chains. The agriculture sector posted record export values in 2025 and continues to serve as a key economic stabilizer. If realized, a sustained surge in agricultural export receipts would meaningfully boost Vietnam's trade surplus and current account balance, providing structural support for VND and contributing positively to foreign reserve accumulation — a direct positive for FX stability.

medium.title: A Change at the Vietnam-China Border Could Determine the Future of Tens of Billions of USD in Vietnamese Agricultural Exports
medium.summary: Vietnam's agricultural export logistics face a critical bottleneck at China border checkpoints, where virtually every shipment of high-value produce such as durian is subject to physical inspection for cadmium, artificial colorants, and heavy metals — driving up costs and clearance times. Officials from the General Department of Customs highlighted these challenges at a government-organized forum on July 9th. The article argues that the solution lies not merely in expanding border infrastructure but in upgrading traceability systems and data-driven risk management. For FX and current account watchers, frictions at the China border represent a tangible drag on export earnings realization speed and could weigh on near-term trade surplus figures if unresolved ahead of peak harvest seasons.

medium.title: BIDV Dividend Record Date & Cash Payout Schedule: Week of July 13–17 — One Major Bank to Distribute Over VND 3,000 Billion
medium.summary: Approximately 40 companies will set dividend record dates during the week of July 13–17, with around 30 paying cash dividends ranging from 2% to 50%. The headline item is **BIDV (ticker: BID, HOSE)**, which will set its record date on July 20 for a 4.5% cash dividend on 2025 earnings (VND 450 per share). With over 7.28 billion shares outstanding, BIDV's total cash outlay will exceed **VND 3,276 billion (~USD 128 million)**; payment is scheduled for August 20. Separately, BIDV's board has approved a bonus share issuance of approximately 498.2 million shares (~6.84% of outstanding shares) to increase charter capital, expected in Q2–Q3 2026. For equity investors in the banking sector, this dual action — cash dividend plus capital increase — is relevant to BIDV's capital adequacy trajectory and its ability to support loan growth. The ex-dividend date of July 17 may create mild near-term selling pressure on BID shares.

medium.title: 20 Years of VSDC Development: Step by Step Bringing Vietnam's Securities Market Closer to International Standards
medium.summary: The Vietnam Securities Depository and Clearing Corporation (VSDC) celebrated its 20th anniversary (founded July 7, 2006) on July 11, attended by senior government officials including the Deputy Minister of Finance and the Chairman of the State Securities Commission. The event underscored VSDC's role as the critical market infrastructure institution ensuring safe, transparent, and efficient operation of Vietnam's capital markets. In the context of Vietnam's upcoming FTSE Russell emerging market upgrade in September 2026, the continued modernization of settlement and clearing infrastructure at VSDC is directly relevant to international investors' ability to access Vietnamese markets at scale. Improvements in post-trade infrastructure reduce operational risk for foreign funds and support the case for sustained capital inflows into Vietnamese equities and bonds.

medium.title: SJC Gold Bar and Plain Gold Ring Prices — Afternoon of July 11
medium.summary: SJC gold bars were quoted at VND 146.9–149.9 million/tael on July 11, with plain gold rings at VND 146.6–149.6 million/tael. Bao Tin Manh Hai made a sharp upward adjustment on July 10 before holding prices steady on the morning of July 11. Internationally, spot gold traded around USD 4,119/oz, little changed over the prior 24 hours, as rising U.S. Treasury yields and sustained Fed rate-hold expectations offset support from a weaker dollar and Hormuz Strait geopolitical risk. Gold and silver prices dipped in late Friday U.S. trading, with sentiment still mixed following the June U.S. jobs report and the recently released Fed meeting minutes.

medium.title: Vietnam Surpasses China, Receives Very Good News in the U.S. Market
medium.summary: Vietnam's footwear exports generated over USD 2.1 billion in May 2026, with cumulative 5-month exports reaching USD 9.78 billion (+0.18% YoY). The headline positive is Vietnam's outperformance in the U.S. market specifically, where footwear exports rose 5.94% YoY to USD 3.79 billion — accounting for nearly 39% of total footwear exports and suggesting Vietnam continues to capture market share, potentially at China's expense amid ongoing U.S.-China trade tensions. The Netherlands (USD 792M, +7%) and Belgium (USD 480M, -4%) rank as the second and third largest export destinations respectively. For FX and macro watchers, this is a modestly supportive data point for Vietnam's trade balance and USD inflow dynamics. Sustained export momentum in the U.S. market could provide a modest tailwind for VND stability, as export dollar receipts help offset import pressures. However, the slight MoM and YoY declines in May warrant monitoring for any signs of demand softening heading into H2 2026.

medium.title: Which Country Holds the Most Gold in the World Today?
medium.summary: Global central banks resumed gold purchases in May 2026, according to World Gold Council (WGC) data cited by The Nation. Poland led with 18 tonnes added in May, followed by China (10 tonnes), Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, and notably Singapore — which returned as a net buyer with 4 tonnes, its first net monthly purchase since September 2025. Year-to-date through mid-2026, Poland has accumulated 64 tonnes, followed by Uzbekistan (33t), China (25t), and Kazakhstan (20t). The US remains the world's largest gold holder at 8,133.5 tonnes. The top 10 nations collectively hold approximately 70% of global gold reserves.
